name: Bar Restaurante El Cine
description: A cosy, no-frills classic by Los Cristianos harbour serving honest traditional Canarian cooking — especially fresh fish — at very reasonable prices (~€10–20 a head). A local favourite for an easy, tasty, wallet-friendly meal.

name: Pescaito Los Cristianos
description: A bustling, well-priced fish spot loved by locals and visitors alike — generous plates of fresh, simply-done seafood at gentle prices (~€15–20 a head). Great for a relaxed, no-fuss lunch or dinner.

name: El Ventorrillo
description: A buzzing little tavern in the pedestrian old streets of Los Cristianos, rustic Canarian decor and generous, honest plates. Famous for its grilled octopus. Where local families actually eat — great value at ~€20–30 a head.
meetingPoint: P.º Dulce María Loinaz 18, Los Cristianos

name: Taberna Vasca Txupinazo
description: A Basque tavern a couple of streets back from the front in Los Cristianos, raved about for food, service and atmosphere. Their cachopo won the national 'best in the Canaries' contest. ~€20–30 per person — book ahead, it fills up.

name: Quei Bravi Ragazzi
description: An elegant, highly-rated Italian doing refined fresh pasta and a serious wine list — a step up for a special dinner in Los Cristianos (~€40–55 a head). Polished service and a romantic feel; book ahead.

name: Restaurante Qapaq
description: Beautifully presented Peruvian cooking — vibrant ceviches and Nikkei plates that stand out from the usual. One of the highest-rated tables in Los Cristianos for a creative, upscale evening (~€40–50 a head).

name: The Palms Fish & Chips
description: A proper, well-rated British chippy for when you fancy a comforting, cheap bite (~€10–15 a head). Big portions, crisp batter — an easy family-friendly stop in Las Américas.

name: Limonella
description: A perennial favourite for proper wood-fired pizza and pasta at friendly prices (~€15–20 a head). Reliable, generous and family-friendly — one of the most-reviewed spots in Las Américas for a reason.

name: Thai Botánico
description: Hugely popular authentic Thai spot in CC Safari, with thousands of glowing reviews and a lush, leafy setting. A welcome change from seafood-and-steak when you fancy bold, fragrant flavours. Mid-range prices.
meetingPoint: CC Safari, 1st floor, Av. de las Américas, Playa de las Américas

name: La Medusa
description: A stylish, very well-rated Mediterranean-seafood table for a relaxed mid-range dinner (~€30–40 a head). Fresh fish done with care and a buzzy atmosphere — book for evenings.

name: The Bank Steak House
description: Stylish East-Coast-inspired steakhouse inside Hotel Villa Cortés on the seafront. Premium cuts cooked precisely, polished service, chic room — a reliable upscale dinner (~€45–60 a head).
meetingPoint: Av. Rafael Puig Lluvina 38, Hotel Villa Cortés, Playa de las Américas

name: Uluwatu — Asian Peruvian Grill
description: A sleek, creative Asian-Peruvian grill for a standout night out — bold Nikkei plates and robata-grilled dishes, beautifully presented (~€45–60 a head). One of the trendiest upscale tables in Las Américas; book ahead.

name: Restaurante Pizzería San Marco
description: A dependable, long-running Italian doing proper wood-fired pizza and pasta at easy prices (~€12–18 a head). Friendly and family-friendly — a safe budget bet in Costa Adeje.

name: Pizzeria Originale
description: A small, genuinely-Italian pizzeria turning out excellent Neapolitan pizza at gentle prices (~€12–18 a head). Cosy and authentic — great for an unfussy family meal.

name: Almar Tenerife
description: A bright, very popular seafood-Mediterranean spot for a relaxed mid-range meal (~€30–40 a head). Fresh fish and rice dishes done well; one of the most-reviewed tables in Costa Adeje.

name: Restaurante Donaire
description: Boldly reinterpreted Canarian flavours in a smart contemporary setting — creative and beautifully plated, yet still mid-range (~€30–40 a head). A standout for foodies in Costa Adeje; book ahead.

name: Bésame Mucho
description: An upmarket seafood-and-grill house for a treat dinner — top-quality fish and meat off the grill in a stylish room (~€45–60 a head). Reliably excellent; book for the evening.

name: La Cúpula Restaurant
description: An elegant fusion fine-dining room for a memorable evening — inventive plates and a refined setting (~€55–70 a head). A polished step-up choice when you want to mark the occasion.

name: San Hô
description: One Michelin star (Guide España 2025), inside the Royal Hideaway Corales Beach in La Caleta. Chef Adrián Bosch blends Japan, Peru and the Canaries into a refined tasting-menu experience (~€120 pp). For a once-in-a-trip splurge.
meetingPoint: Av. Virgen de Guadalupe 21, Royal Hideaway Corales Beach, La Caleta, Adeje

name: Tas-K
description: A tiny, much-loved tapas bar a few metres from the beach — widely called the best tapas in Los Gigantes. ~€5 a tapa with 4-for-€10 deals (~€10–20 a head). Small and popular, so book ahead.
meetingPoint: Just off the beach, Los Gigantes

name: Restaurante Pizzería Mamma Lucia
description: A friendly, well-rated Italian for a budget-friendly family meal in Los Gigantes (~€15–20 a head). Generous wood-fired pizzas and pasta; easy and reliable.

name: Casa Edu
description: A hugely popular local grill near Playa de la Arena — generous portions of well-cooked meat and Spanish classics at fair prices (~€25–30 a head). Thousands of happy reviews; book at peak times.
meetingPoint: Playa de la Arena, Los Gigantes

name: Sargo Restaurante
description: A polished but relaxed Mediterranean-seafood spot doing fresh fish and Italian-leaning plates very well (~€25–35 a head). Consistently top-rated in Los Gigantes for a mid-range dinner.

name: KV Bar Gourmet
description: An intimate harbourside bistro facing the boats and the famous cliffs, doing innovative homemade French-leaning cooking (~€40–55 a head). A touch pricier than its neighbours but consistently the best plate in Los Gigantes.

name: Cielo y Mar
description: An upscale Spanish-seafood table with lovely views for a special evening in Los Gigantes (~€40–55 a head). Carefully cooked fresh fish and a calm, romantic setting; book ahead.

name: Casa Mary
description: A no-frills local institution in Las Galletas with a near-perfect rating from thousands of guests. Generous home-style Spanish cooking at very gentle prices (~€10–20 a head) — exactly where locals go.

name: Restaurante Euro
description: A friendly budget pizzeria in Las Galletas with a loyal local following — tasty wood-fired pizza and pasta at very fair prices (~€10–18 a head). Easy and family-friendly.

name: Restaurante Varadero Viejo
description: A beloved seafront seafood house in the laid-back fishing town of Las Galletas — one of the highest ratings in the whole south. Honest portions of properly fresh fish at fair prices (~€25–35 a head).

name: Restaurant Fish-Art
description: A warmly-run European-seafood restaurant in Costa del Silencio with thousands of glowing reviews — fresh fish, careful cooking and friendly service at mid-range prices (~€25–35 a head).

name: Bouganville Ristorante
description: A smart, well-loved Italian in Costa del Silencio for a step-up dinner (~€35–45 a head). Fresh handmade pasta and a proper wine list in an elegant setting; book for the evening.

name: Viento Sur
description: A refined French-European table for a special, grown-up dinner in Costa del Silencio (~€40–55 a head). Classic technique, careful service and a calm room; book ahead.

name: Pangea Restaurant
description: A lively, well-priced Mexican spot in Puerto de la Cruz — fresh tacos and cocktails in a fun atmosphere (~€12–20 a head). Great for a casual, cheerful bite. Note: Puerto is ~1h north.

name: Señorita Canelita
description: A charming, great-value little spot in Puerto de la Cruz beloved for brunch and casual Spanish-European plates (~€12–20 a head). Pretty, friendly and easy on the wallet. Note: Puerto is ~1h north.

name: Arcón Tapas
description: A favourite for authentic Canarian tapas by Plaza del Charco in Puerto de la Cruz. Famous for some of the best papas arrugadas and mojo on the island (~€20–30 a head). Note: Puerto is ~1h north.
meetingPoint: Near Plaza del Charco, Puerto de la Cruz

name: Ibéricos Gastro-bar
description: A stylish, top-rated gastro-bar in Puerto de la Cruz serving creative Mediterranean-Spanish small plates and good wines (~€25–35 a head). Buzzy and modern; book at peak times. Note: Puerto is ~1h north.

name: Longo Steak House
description: A well-regarded steakhouse in Puerto de la Cruz for a hearty upscale dinner (~€40–55 a head). Quality cuts cooked properly in a smart setting; book ahead. Note: Puerto is ~1h north.

name: El Taller Seve Díaz
description: A Michelin-starred kitchen in Puerto de la Cruz where chef Seve Díaz turns local and Mediterranean produce into refined, creative dishes (~€60–80 a head). A north-coast destination for a special meal. Note: Puerto is ~1h north.

name: Guachinche Como En Casa
description: A classic Canarian guachinche near La Laguna — home-style grilled meats and local wine at rock-bottom prices (~€10–18 a head), with a huge local following. As authentic as it gets. Note: La Laguna is ~50 min north.

name: La Perla Negra
description: A buzzy, great-value pizza-and-American spot in La Laguna with thousands of reviews — big portions, easy prices (~€12–18 a head). Reliable for a casual, filling meal. Note: La Laguna is ~50 min north.

name: La Tasca Faracho
description: A tiny, characterful tapas tavern in a colonial house in La Laguna's UNESCO old town — only seven tables and outstanding traditional Canarian small plates (~€25–30 a head). Book ahead. Note: La Laguna is ~50 min north.
meetingPoint: Calle Santo Domingo, historic centre, La Laguna

name: Fusión Vinos y Tapas
description: A stylish wine-and-tapas spot in La Laguna's old town serving creative small plates with a strong Canarian wine list (~€25–30 a head). Intimate and relaxed; book ahead. Note: La Laguna is ~50 min north.

name: Restaurante Maquila
description: One of La Laguna's top tables — contemporary Canarian-Spanish cooking from quality market produce, beautifully done (~€45–60 a head). A destination dinner in the historic city. Note: La Laguna is ~50 min north.

name: Big Nonna Tenerife
description: A stylish, top-rated Italian in La Laguna for a special evening — fresh handmade pasta and a confident wine list in a chic room (~€40–55 a head). Book ahead. Note: La Laguna is ~50 min north.
